facts.old: Pointwise: absolute scale, for monitoring and gating, no baseline

facts.old: Pointwise weakness: scale drift (7/10 today is not 7/10 next month or on another judge)

facts.old: Fine-grained scales are noise past about 4 distinguishable levels

facts.old: Binary forces the rubric author to decide what failure means
facts.where: rd-design Pointwise, Hamel quote

facts.old: Pairwise: A vs B optionally tie; higher human agreement than pointwise for open-ended quality
facts.where: rd-design Pairwise; nuanced: on MT-Bench the same 10 pairs give 69.2% vs 68.4% (kappa 0.355 vs 0.351), so not higher there; Tripathi et al. distractor result added

facts.old: Pairwise right mode for model-swap decisions
facts.where: rd-design Pairwise; rd-one table

facts.old: Pairwise weaknesses: position bias (both orders), tie inflation, O(n^2) cost
facts.where: rd-design Pairwise (n(n-1)/2 per prompt, twice with both orders; baseline design); tie inflation measured in the Protocol lab (9.8% to 20.3%)

facts.old: Rubric/reference-guided: most reliable when references exist; cuts hallucinated judgments on math/code

facts.old: Position bias: judge model choice affects it more than task type or quality gap

facts.where: rd-bias table (65.0% hardest case, 83.6% ordinary)

facts.old: Position mitigation: both orders, disagreements as ties (or resample); never single order
facts.where: rd-bias table; rd-ops 2; Protocol lab measures the gain

facts.old: Verbosity bias: longer answers win independent of quality

facts.old: Self-preference: Panickssery arXiv:2404.13076 linear relation between self-recognition and self-preference
facts.where: rd-bias table; t-more

facts.old: Self-preference mitigation: never judge with itself or a sibling across families; third family or jury
facts.where: rd-bias table; rd-ops 6; Calibration lab GPT-4 specificity 0.37

facts.old: Sycophancy / authority bias: confident tone, citations (even fake), assertive framing raise scores
facts.where: rd-bias table: Authority (CALM 0.662 to 0.865, quote/book vs URL) and Bandwagon; note that 'confident tone' has no clean single measurement

facts.old: Format exploitation: null model 86.5% LC AlpacaEval 2.0, 83.0 Arena-Hard-Auto, exploiting template parsing, embedded instructions
facts.where: rd-exploit table (plus 76.9 raw, 9.55 MT-Bench, structured-only figures)

facts.old: Any judge pipeline feeding candidate text into a template is prompt-injectable
facts.where: rd-exploit closing paragraph

facts.old: Mitigation: delimit candidate text, treat as data, injection canaries
facts.where: rd-exploit; rd-prompt; rd-ops 4 (with the paper's failed defences added)

facts.old: Re-check on fresh samples for drift

facts.where: rd-cal and rd-one corrections: 63% with ties, 81% without (MT-Bench experts)

facts.old: A judge at 80% with one human may be at ceiling
facts.where: rd-cal kappa paragraph; Protocol lab shows judge at or above the human-human tick

facts.old: PoLL: jury of smaller judges from different families, mean or vote, better human correlation than one GPT-4 judge at roughly 7-8x lower cost, washes out intra-family bias
facts.where: rd-jury (Command R, Haiku, GPT-3.5; max voting vs average pooling; kappa 0.763 vs 0.627; Pearson 0.917 vs 0.817; 'over seven times less expensive'; Haiku alone 0.749 caveat)

facts.old: PoLL is the default pattern for production judge batteries
facts.where: rd-jury and rd-ops 6, with scope caveat

facts.old: Robust aggregation: plain mean fragile; RoPoLL arXiv:2606.30931 geometric median; median or trimmed mean; monitor per-juror agreement
facts.where: rd-jury (Huber contamination, unbounded bias, 13 judges, 19%, 1.31x, Gaussian-noise caveat)

facts.old: Debate / meta-judge (ChatEval) buys a few points at large cost; only for offline audits
